symptoms: A cache or session-store node is pegged at high CPU or memory, causing downstream request failures or timeouts on services that depend on it.
action: Cordon and restart the affected cache node; downstream connections re-pool automatically.
expectedOutcome: CPU on the affected node drops back under 40% within a few minutes, and the downstream error rate returns to baseline.

symptoms: Web or API tier request latency or error rate is climbing under load, with healthy downstream dependencies (databases, caches) and no single failing node.
action: Increase the web tier's replica count by 50% to spread load.
expectedOutcome: Per-instance CPU and request latency drop as load spreads across more replicas within a couple of minutes.

symptoms: A message queue or job queue is backing up, with consumers falling behind and processing latency growing.
action: Temporarily add extra consumer workers to drain the backlog.
expectedOutcome: Queue depth falls back toward zero and processing latency returns to normal within 10-15 minutes.

symptoms: A credential or access key appears compromised or is being misused (e.g. anomalous access patterns, leaked secret).
action: Revoke the credential and rotate it to a new value across all consuming services.
expectedOutcome: Anomalous access from the old credential stops immediately; services must be redeployed or reloaded with the new credential.
